ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify whether PLPC products are embedded in utility standards, EPC approved-vendor lists, RFPs, or engineering drawings; quantify energy revenue mix, backlog growth, customer concentration, margin durability, and whether grid-related orders are accelerating.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary evidence from 10-K/10-Q, investor materials, utility standards, procurement records, customer references, and backlog/order commentary proving that grid-related demand is material and accelerating rather than merely thematically adjacent.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Highest Serenity priority because the company maps to a narrow, mandatory, low-glamour bill-of-materials layer in transmission and distribution: line hardware, fittings, motion-control, protection, splicing, and termination products. The demand driver is durable if grid expansion, grid hardening, renewable interconnection, and AI/data-center load growth translate into physical line construction. The underfollowed setup is strong because the candidate sits below utilities, EPCs, transformer makers, and mega-cap electrical OEMs.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Often screened as an obscure electrical hardware manufacturer rather than a critical grid-buildout supplier. External context claims limited Wall Street coverage and long-lived utility specification positioning, which creates a clear hidden-signal path but still requires primary-source verification.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Check DOE awards, HALEU contract status, enrichment licensing, production capacity, technology readiness, cash conversion, Russian-enrichment exposure, customer commitments, and whether policy awards translate into profitable revenue.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need verification that DOE negotiations, contingent order book, and policy support convert into funded, scalable, profitable domestic enrichment capacity rather than remaining long-duration optionality.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Ranks high because enrichment and HALEU are potentially severe nuclear fuel-cycle chokepoints with policy support, long qualification timelines, national-security relevance, and limited public-market ways to express the theme. External context indicates Centrus presents itself as the only publicly traded deployment-ready U.S. enricher positioned for LEU and HALEU markets, with a large order book including contingent sales.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Known among nuclear specialists but less obvious to generalist energy investors than uranium miners, utilities, SMR developers, or IPPs. The hidden angle is that the chokepoint may be enrichment, conversion, HALEU, licensing, and fuel fabrication rather than raw uranium mining.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Validate transformer and power-quality revenue mix, backlog, lead times, pricing power, customer mix, AEG Power Solutions integration, data-center exposure, and whether growth is tied to durable electrification demand rather than temporary distributor restocking.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary filings and management commentary separating durable end-market demand from distributor restocking, price/cost timing, and acquisition-related growth.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Strong Serenity candidate because dry-type transformers, power-quality equipment, and magnetics are close to durable electrification, digital infrastructure, microgrid, renewables, industrial, transportation, and semiconductor power-distribution demand. The thesis is highly falsifiable through backlog, lead times, pricing, margins, segment disclosures, and customer mix.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Less obscure after rerating, but still can be misclassified as a boring transformer company rather than a broader power-infrastructure and power-quality supplier. It is underfollowed relative to mega-cap electrical equipment leaders.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify IPO filings, annual report, order book, margin profile, export mix, named customer evidence, 800 kV HVDC reactor orders, Microsoft Finland data-center reference, certifications, qualification cycles, and whether customer names represent direct sales, indirect supply, or historical relationships.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary documents proving revenue quality, export/customer claims, order-book conversion, certification depth, and whether named global customers represent current material business.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: High-priority underfollowed candidate because the company maps to specialized high-voltage equipment and power-quality nodes: HVDC, FACTS, reactors, harmonic filters, STATCOM, and smart-grid solutions. These nodes can become bottlenecks in renewable integration, long-distance bulk power transfer, industrial electrification, and data-center power quality.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: India-listed niche supplier with messy classification and limited global investor mindshare compared with Siemens, GE Vernova, Hitachi Energy, and ABB. The obscurity is attractive only if order book, certifications, and customer evidence prove real supplier qualification.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Validate backlog, book-to-bill, data-center and utility exposure, switchgear lead times, gross margin sustainability, customer concentration, and whether recent growth is cyclical energy capex or durable electrification demand.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need proof that recent demand and margin expansion are tied to durable electrical infrastructure bottlenecks rather than temporary energy capex cycles, project mix, or price/cost benefits.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Attractive follow-up candidate because engineered power distribution, switchgear, and control gear can become lead-time bottlenecks for industrial electrification, data centers, utility infrastructure, and energy projects. The research path is concrete: backlog, book-to-bill, gross margin, segment mix, and customer exposure can confirm or reject the thesis.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Often categorized as cyclical energy or industrial electrical equipment rather than as a second-order beneficiary of power scarcity, grid constraints, and data-center electrical buildout.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Review Meyer Utility Structures revenue contribution, backlog by end market, transmission project exposure, margin trend, capex, customer concentration, and whether steel or concrete pole manufacturing capacity is becoming a constraint.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segment-level evidence showing utility structures are large enough and growing enough to matter to consolidated results.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Good adjacent-chokepoint candidate through engineered utility structures, including transmission, distribution, and substation structures. The grid-buildout linkage is plausible and testable, especially if Meyer Utility Structures has material exposure to transmission capex and grid-hardening projects.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Usually screened as general infrastructure or construction materials rather than as a grid hardware supplier. Utility structures may be hidden within a diversified infrastructure-products business.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Check infrastructure end-market mix, utility T&D customer evidence, galvanizing utilization, regional capacity near transmission-structure fabricators, pricing power, and whether electrical infrastructure is material versus general industrial demand.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that utility and grid infrastructure represent a material and accelerating demand source, not just a broad industrial correlation.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Strong second-order research candidate because hot-dip galvanizing and corrosion protection can be required for outdoor steel structures and components used in transmission, distribution, substations, and other electrical infrastructure. The underfollowed angle is high, but the chokepoint is one step removed from visible T&D demand.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Usually screened as industrial coatings or metal services, not as a grid-expansion supplier. Energy exposure can sit through fabricators, pole makers, structure makers, and outdoor infrastructure customers rather than direct utility disclosures.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Determine whether utility solutions orders, pricing, and margins are being specifically driven by transmission rebuilds, interconnection queues, grid hardening, and AI/data-center load growth versus general electrical demand.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Lower discovery value because the company is larger and better understood; need segment-specific proof to avoid confusing general electrification exposure with a narrow bottleneck.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Useful reference leader for utility-qualified line construction hardware, connectors, pole-line hardware, and broader utility solutions. It helps benchmark pricing, margins, demand commentary, approved-vendor dynamics, and product breadth for smaller candidates such as PLPC.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed at the company level. Included because utility hardware and line-construction components can be hidden inside a diversified electrical products franchise.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify utility structures revenue mix, backlog, project wins, capacity, margin trend, exposure to transmission and substation work, and whether grid-related demand is large enough to affect consolidated growth.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segment-level data proving that grid infrastructure demand is material, accelerating, and not offset by unrelated cyclical segments.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Included as a useful infrastructure and utility-structure benchmark. The transmission, distribution, lighting, pole, and engineered-structures angle may benefit from grid hardening and electrification capex, but public-market purity is likely diluted by broader infrastructure and agriculture exposures.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not highly underfollowed relative to smaller niche suppliers, but the utility-structure exposure may be overlooked when the company is screened as a diversified infrastructure and agricultural equipment supplier.
